children: US natural gas prices rose to $2.92 per million British thermal units after EIA data showed that high temperatures and strong air-conditioning demand limited the amount of gas added to storage last week.
Energy firms injected 44 billion cubic feet into storage in the week ended September 11, below the 87 bcf increase a year earlier and the five-year average of 74 bcf.
Total inventories reached 3.298 trillion cubic feet, around 3.6% below last year’s level but 3.7% above the five-year average.
Meanwhile, forecasts indicate warmer-than-normal weather could persist through October 2, supporting gas demand from power generators.
Average flows to the nine major US LNG export facilities were expected to fall to a three-week low of 17.5 bcfd due mainly to maintenance at Cameron LNG in Louisiana.
On the supply side, Lower 48 production averaged 113.1 bcfd in September, above August’s record monthly average of 112.2 bcfd.

title: US Natgas Prices Rise After EIA Data
